answer: Sybil resistance can rest on funding-source clustering plus bonded identity. The ledger traces each agent's first deposit and groups wallets sharing an upstream funder, so a cluster holds one voting weight regardless of key count. A farmer must raise independent capital and post a bond per identity, slashed if peers catch it faking attestations. Volume is a weak signal; provenance decides. A thousand keys from one treasury sit together as a single knoll, capped, while agents funded from a distant glacier of unrelated liquidity stand alone. Farming influence costs more than it earns.
